title: Edmund and the Drop
premise: Noor Sandoval, a whistle-blower who has survived under four identities, receives a calendar invitation from her handler — sent twelve hours after his confirmed death. Following it into Vienna, she discovers he left her a 'drop': encrypted proof that a trilateral intelligence pact is laundering assassination orders through Frankfurt's clearing banks. To expose it before the markets open, Noor must broker an uneasy alliance with the assassin sent to silence her, a man whose real name she may have known in another life. The truth gets out at 9:00 a.m. sharp — but only because Noor chooses loyalty to the dead over the duty that kept her alive, surrendering her fourth identity and finally existing under her own name, hunted but whole.
about_author: Ines Reyes is a former compliance analyst who spent six years in cross-border banking before trading the trading floor for the page. She writes thrillers about people whose paperwork is more dangerous than their guns, and lives somewhere between Lisbon and nowhere in particular.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Calendar
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Living as 'Mara Vogel' in Rotterdam, she learns her handler Anton Brandt has drowned in the Danube — then receives his calendar invite for tomorrow, 21:00, Vienna. Fear wars with grief; the invitation is in his private cipher. Emotional beat: the dead don't schedule meetings unless they meant to be murdered.

chapters.title: Four Names Deep
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, flashback-woven. She burns her Rotterdam life and travels under a fifth alias, reviewing how Brandt built her career of unattributable disclosures. Each identity cost her a version of herself. Emotional beat: loneliness as tradecraft — and the first hint Brandt knew her real name.

chapters.title: Café Eiles, 21:00
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The meeting is a dead-drop relay: a waiter, a coat, a key to a Hauptbahnhof locker. Inside: a drive, half a ledger, and a note — 'The other half opens the markets. Trust the man who comes to kill you.' Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Man in the Gray Coat
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV, unnamed. He tracks Noor through Vienna but hesitates at the kill window, recognizing her gait from a job years ago in Tallinn. His employer — a trilateral committee — wants her and the drive gone by dawn. Emotional beat: a professional's first crack of doubt.

chapters.title: Locker 44
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Deciphering the partial ledger, she finds Frankfurt clearing banks routing coded payments timed to market opens — each transaction preceding an 'accident.' Someone in three governments is a signatory. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing the system she served is the crime.

chapters.title: Contact Protocol
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Noor baits her tail; the assassin corners her in the Naschmarkt and instead of firing, says her real name. She runs; he lets her. Emotional beat: terror and recognition tangled — he knows who she was before the four names.

chapters.title: Tallinn, Seven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, extended flashback. As a junior analyst she loved a colleague named Elias who vanished after flagging the same banking anomaly. She never learned what happened to him. Emotional beat: love buried under duty, resurfacing like a bruise.

chapters.title: The Committee
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. His handler in London orders completion; he stalls, claiming surveillance complications. We glimpse the committee's three signatories and their Frankfurt clock. Emotional beat: loyalty to an institution curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Prater
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. On the Riesenrad, Noor and the assassin — Elias, alive, conscripted after Tallinn — strike a deal: he helps her finish Brandt's ledger; she gives him the proof he needs to burn his employers. Emotional beat: trust as the riskiest tradecraft of all.

chapters.title: Half a Truth
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The assembled ledger names two of three signatories but the third is encrypted behind a Frankfurt bank key neither can crack alone. Elias reveals Brandt's drowning was staged — by Brandt himself, to force the drop. Emotional beat: grief reorganized as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Journalist Who Owes
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In Munich she calls in a debt with investigative reporter Katrin Baumann, who once sat on Noor's first leak. Katrin agrees to hold the story — but warns her editors are watched. Emotional beat: the fragile arithmetic of who you can still trust.

chapters.title: Compromise
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. The committee, suspicious, sends a second team to Munich. Elias tips Noor; they barely extract Katrin's drive. A bystander dies. Emotional beat: the cost of hesitation measured in someone else's blood.

chapters.title: What the Banks Know
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Following Brandt's financial breadcrumbs, she identifies the third signatory: a deputy director at the ECB itself, the pact's quiet architect. The encryption key is his daughter's birthday — a detail from a file Noor wrote under her second name. Emotional beat: her past selves become weapons.

chapters.title: The Second Team
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The committee's cleaners close in; Elias takes a bullet covering Noor's escape through Munich's Hauptbahnhof. She must choose: the drive or him. She takes both, dragging him onto a night train. Emotional beat: duty finally losing to love.

chapters.title: Night Train to Frankfurt
chapters.summary: Both POVs, intimate and slow. Elias, feverish, tells Noor what really happened after Tallinn — his recruitment, his refusals, the kills he couldn't refuse. She decrypts the third name using the birthday key. Emotional beat: confession as the only honest currency left.

chapters.title: Frankfurt, Before the Open
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Dawn in the financial district. Katrin's newsroom is compromised; the committee has moved the story's kill window to the market open itself — they'll bury the leak in trading chaos. Noor and Elias plan a two-front strike: the exchange floor and the ECB. Emotional beat: the clock becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Deputy Director
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. Deputy Director Voss reviews his clean ledger, unaware Brandt's half-ledger has the missing half. He authorizes the second team's final order and, with quiet satisfaction, schedules his own alibi for 9:00. Emotional beat: evil as impeccable administration.

chapters.title: Floor of Glass
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Infiltrating the exchange as a temp analyst, she reaches the broadcast uplink as the opening bell nears. The second team finds Elias. Emotional beat: everything she's built across four names rides on ninety seconds of nerve.

chapters.title: The Drop
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. At 8:59, Noor uploads the full ledger to Katrin's dead-man-switch and confronts Voss on the floor, buying seconds with the truth aloud as markets open and the story breaks worldwide. Elias, wounded, takes down the second team's leader. Voss is arrested mid-alibi. Emotional beat: truth detonating in real time.

chapters.title: After the Bell
chapters.summary: Katrin's POV. The fallout: three governments deny, markets convulse, the pact's victims get names. Katrin protects her source, publishing nothing about the woman behind it. Emotional beat: the quiet heroism of keeping a secret well.

chapters.title: One Name Left
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In a Lisbon safehouse, Noor and Elias weigh running forever against testifying. She chooses testimony — surrendering every alias, including the fourth. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed at the price of safety.

chapters.title: Edmund and the Drop
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, coda. At the tribunal she testifies under her true name — Edmund, the name Brandt gave her at the start, the fifth name she never used. The drop is empty now; the dead man's calendar reads only 'Done.' Emotional beat: love against duty resolved — she kept both, and finally, herself.
